g.text: C344 · Monolithic lasers: the promise, and how laser thresholds fell

g.text: Book Sec. 8.5 (p. 303) · gain material grown directly on silicon would be highly advantageous; the history of III-V lasers [30] is a useful guide

g.text: 1 · Threshold current density of III-V lasers

g.text: Book: decades of research took thresholds from >10⁵ A/cm² (currents in the amperes) to <10³ A/cm² (mA devices).

g.text: • undoped → less absorption • small volume → less current

g.text: Book: decades of research were needed to make the III-V laser a practical, efficient device (panels 1–3).

text.style: font-weight: 700; font-size: 8.6px; font-family: 'Inter', 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: middle; fill: #f6f6f6

g.text: Takeaway: an undoped gain layer (DH) and ever smaller gain regions (DH → quantum well → quantum dot) cut the threshold from 10–100 kA/cm² to 16 A/cm².

text.style: font-size: 7.8px; font-family: 'Inter', 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: middle; fill: #a1a1a6

g.text: Monolithic gain on Si would add density, reliability, functionality and low-cost fabrication, but is less mature · Book Sec. 8.5 (p. 303), refs [30]–[32]
